activity.notes: Martin Luther King Jr. emerged as a major civil rights leader when Montgomery's Black community leaders formed the Montgomery Improvement Association on 5 December 1955 and elected him president. He subsequently became a national leader of the nonviolent civil rights movement, including as president of the Southern Christian Leadership Conference from 1957, and remained publicly active in civil rights and social-justice campaigns until his assassination on 4 April 1968. ATLAS uses the United States as the political context with active_in rather than a governance relation, because King sought reform and equal citizenship within the United States rather than ruling a separate polity.
